playbook:
When I can afford a settlement (1 of each resource), I build the settlement rather than a road — settlements give more points for the same number of resources.

When I have exactly one brick and I will not immediately build a settlement or road this round, I do not trade away that brick unless I receive brick back or will gain a build opportunity this round — don’t trade away my only brick.

When I lack brick and a counterparty has brick, I offer 1 wood for 1 brick (or 1 grain for 1 brick) to acquire brick quickly; prioritize trading expendable resources (extra wood/grain) for brick.

Prefer to give expendable resources in this order: wood > grain > ore, except when wood is required for an immediate build — in that case prefer to give grain (or ore) instead of wood.

When I can build a settlement this round, I post no offers — do not trade away resources that enable an immediate higher-value build.

When I am offered a favorable 1:1 trade that gives me brick (or another needed resource) and accepting it does not leave me unable to build this round or in the next turn window toward my goal, I accept it.

When an offer would leave me unable to reach a clear build goal in the next one or two rounds (e.g., trading away my only brick when a settlement is achievable), I decline it.

When multiple counterparties have the needed resource, prefer trading with the party who has it in surplus or who is less likely to be enabled to build an immediate win from the swap.

When no counterparty has the resource I need (brick), I post no offer rather than overpay or fragment my holdings.

When I can only build a road, build a road only if it meaningfully advances a near-term settlement plan or blocks an opponent; otherwise build none and conserve resources.

Do not assume trading away resources to help opponents is worth it unless the trade directly enables a build for me that increases my score advantage.

1.text:
When I'm dealt starting resources, if I can build a settlement immediately, build it unless doing so leaves me with zero brick and I expect brick will be scarce next rounds; otherwise prefer the settlement for immediate points.

When I can afford a settlement, choose it over a road unless I specifically need a single point to tie/win.

When I'm missing one resource for a desired build, post a 1-for-1 offer to the player who has that resource, offering a resource they need (prioritize giving wood before ore).

When another player posts an offer giving me brick for my ore, accept it if I can spare the ore and it enables me to build on the upcoming build phase—brick is high priority.

When evaluating incoming offers, only accept trades that (a) enable an immediate build that increases my score that round, or (b) clearly set up a guaranteed build next round given known holdings; do not accept trades that leave me unable to build when the trade's goal was to enable building.

When no one currently has brick, post offers to trade ore for brick rather than grain or wood, because securing brick unlocks both roads and settlements; however, prefer to give wood before ore unless wood is scarce for me.

When I lack brick and no one has it, avoid spending my ore on low-value trades that don't get me brick; preserve ore as a trading currency for critical brick trades or future city upgrades.

When I have spare wood and someone else has grain I need for a build, offer 1 wood for 1 grain—wood is easiest to spare early.

If I cannot build this turn and no useful trades are possible, do not force offers; conserve resources and wait for better trading opportunities.

Do not trade away all my ore if doing so prevents accepting good future offers or building an ore-reliant strategy.

If an offer will let me score immediately (settlement/road), prioritize accepting or making that trade even if it costs a resource I might otherwise prefer to keep.

When posting offers, target the player who both (a) holds the needed resource and (b) lacks the resource I am offering; this increases acceptance chance.

When multiple players post identical offers to me, prefer accepting the one that uses a resource I can most spare and that leaves me best positioned to build in the same or next build phase.

Avoid accepting offers that exchange a resource I need for a guaranteed build (e.g., wood needed to finish a settlement) unless the incoming resource immediately completes that build.

If aiming for a city (ore+grain), do not accept trades that remove my only wood/brick if those are needed to secure a nearer settlement point; compare point gain timelines before accepting.

When in doubt between giving wood or ore in a 1-for-1 trade, give wood unless I foresee an ore-heavy build (city) within the next two turns.

2.text:
When I'm able to build a settlement immediately and it yields more points than a road, I build the settlement.

When I have enough ore (>=3) and grain (>=2) to build a city next turn, I do not post offers that would trade away ore or the grain needed for that city.

When another player clearly has the brick I need to build a settlement this round, I offer 1 grain for 1 brick to them.

When I specifically need wood to complete an immediate settlement and a particular player clearly has wood, I offer 1 grain for 1 wood to that player.

When I lack brick and no one obvious has it, I post no offer rather than trade away grain or ore I may need for higher-value builds.

When an incoming offer would give me a resource I need but would require giving away brick that I need to complete a settlement this turn, I refuse it.

When an incoming offer gives me brick (or wood) in exchange for a resource I can spare (not grain or ore if I need those for a city), I accept.

When I have only enough wood+brick for a road but can instead spend my full resource set to make a settlement that scores more now, I choose the settlement.

When I'm low on wood and brick and can't build, I avoid trading away ore I might later want for a city; prioritize keeping ore unless a trade clearly enables an immediate higher-point build.

Do not make token offers just to be active; only post an offer when it directly advances a concrete build plan.

Addendum from play: prefer offering grain rather than ore when paying for wood or brick, since I consistently preserved ore to keep city options open.
